## Simulación: efecto de $n$ en la distribución muestral

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4.8
set.seed(123)
# Población: rendimiento de café (Gamma asimétrica), media ≈ 2.5 kg/árbol
pop <- rgamma(100000, shape = 2.5, rate = 1)
mu_pop <- mean(pop)

ns <- c(5, 15, 30, 100)
par(mfrow = c(1, 4), mar = c(4, 3.5, 3.2, 1), family = "sans")

colores <- c("#bfdbfe", "#bbf7d0", "#fef3c7", "#f3e8ff")
lineas  <- c("#1e3a8a", "#15803d", "#b45309", "#6d28d9")

for (i in seq_along(ns)) {
  n <- ns[i]
  medias <- replicate(4000, mean(sample(pop, n)))
  hist(medias, probability = TRUE,
       col = colores[i], border = "white",
       main = paste0("n = ", n),
       sub  = paste0("SE ≈ ", round(sd(pop)/sqrt(n), 3)),
       xlab = expression(bar(x)),
       cex.main = 1.3, cex.sub = 1, cex.lab = 1.1, cex.axis = 1)
  lines(density(medias), lwd = 3, col = lineas[i])
  abline(v = mu_pop, col = "#991b1b", lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  box(col = "gray40")
}
```
